---
title: "How do I estimate a population proportion with an interval?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I estimate a population proportion with an interval?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Identify number of successes and number of independent trials.

2. Check successes are between 0 and n.

3. Use prop.test() and report the confidence level.

## Runnable example

```{r}
successes <- 26; n <- 50
estimate <- prop.test(successes,n,conf.level=.95,correct=FALSE)
print(estimate$estimate)
print(estimate$conf.int)
```

## Interpret the result

The observed rate is 26/50 = 0.52, with an approximate 95% interval. That interval reflects sampling uncertainty under the model.

## Check before using real data

Check how the observations were sampled; for small samples or extreme rates consider binom.test() instead of an approximation.
